title: CTest and a failing build that tells you why
summary: Enable CTest, register a test executable, and make a printed failure fail the test run.

scenario.briefing: The inventory project builds a test executable but never registers it, so CI runs ctest and reports zero tests. Register the test and make a printed failure fail the run.

objectives.description: Register a test executable with CTest.
Explain what ctest executes and reports.
Diagnose a test run that discovers no tests.

hints: CTest only sees tests that CMake registered.
enable_testing belongs in the top-level CMakeLists.
add_test connects a name to a command.
Use set_tests_properties to treat a printed failure as a failure.

misconceptions.description: Assuming add_executable also registers a test.
misconceptions.testDescription: The test is registered with a name and command.
misconceptions.feedback: A target builds a binary. add_test tells CTest which command to run and what to call the result.

misconceptions.testDescription: CTest is enabled at the top level.
misconceptions.feedback: enable_testing activates test discovery for the directory. Without it, add_test has no CTest configuration to write.

misconceptions.description: Expecting ctest to compile the test target.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Selecting the statement that ctest compiles the project before running tests.
misconceptions.feedback: ctest runs commands that already exist. Build first, then run ctest, or use ctest --build-and-test for a combined flow.

misconceptions.description: Registering tests only in a subdirectory and expecting the top level to discover them.
misconceptions.feedback: The top-level project must enable testing so CTest has a configuration. Put enable_testing in the top-level CMakeLists.

sections.title: CTest is a runner, not a compiler
sections.body: CMake writes test metadata when it configures the project. ctest reads that metadata and runs the registered commands. A test executable still has to be built by the normal build step, so CI usually runs cmake --build build and then ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure.

sections.title: Registration connects a name to a command
sections.body: add_test(NAME inventory_tests COMMAND inventory_tests) records a test named inventory_tests that runs the executable. The name is what ctest reports and what -R filters match. A target built in another directory can still be run as a command.

sections.title: A zero exit code is not always enough
sections.body: CTest treats a nonzero process exit as a failure. Some test binaries print FAILED and still exit 0. FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION marks the test failed when that text appears, so the runner and the test binary agree.

steps.title: Register the CTest case
steps.prompt: Edit CMakeLists.txt. Enable testing at the top level, register inventory_tests, and fail the test when its output contains FAILED.
hints: Keep the existing test executable and link.
Use add_test with NAME and COMMAND both set to inventory_tests.

files.content:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(campus_inventory LANGUAGES CXX)

add_library(inventory_core STATIC src/inventory.cpp)
target_include_directories(inventory_core PUBLIC include)

# TODO: register the unit test with CTest
add_executable(inventory_tests tests/inventory_test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(inventory_tests PRIVATE inventory_core)

steps.title: What CTest actually does
hints: Separate configure, build, and test phases.
CTest reads metadata that CMake wrote.
The test process exit status is the primary signal.

statements.label: ctest runs commands that CMake registered during configure.
A nonzero exit status from a test command is reported as a failure.
FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION can fail a test even when the process exits 0.
ctest compiles the project before it runs the tests.
add_test builds the named target automatically.

steps.explanation: ctest is a runner over configured metadata. It does not compile sources or build add_test targets. Exit status and configured output properties decide the result.

steps.title: Transfer to a silent CI run
steps.prompt: A project calls add_test in a subdirectory, but the top-level CMakeLists never calls enable_testing. CI runs ctest and reports no tests. What is the cause?
hints: add_test writes metadata only where testing is enabled.
The top-level directory controls the CTest configuration.
A subdirectory call does not retroactively enable the parent.
Move enable_testing to the top-level file.

quiz.prompt: A project calls add_test in a subdirectory, but the top-level CMakeLists never calls enable_testing. CI runs ctest and reports no tests. What is the cause?

options.label: enable_testing is missing at the top level, so CTest has no test configuration.
The subdirectory registration is enough; ctest just needs a rebuild.
ctest cannot compile the test target, so it hides the test.
add_test requires a TEST_NAME property that the subdirectory omitted.

quiz.explanation: CTest metadata is generated where testing is enabled. The top-level project needs enable_testing before ctest can discover the registered tests.

accessibility.summary: The workspace is keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure and the reference tests; they do not compile or run the framework.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between the editor and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, whether it passed, and the missing or forbidden source fragment or test failure.
